title: A saturated video is sent whole, however big it is (R1008 slice 1)
body:
Slice 1 of `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` — **OD-13**, **R28**, **R1008**. The slug is an ADDRESS, not a description: that plan was rewritten on 2026-08-20 and specifies the **uncapped** path.

### What it does

`submission.py` is new. `choose_submission` compares the saturation ratio and **nothing else** — that is the whole of OD-13. A three-hour saturated stream goes whole exactly as a thirty-minute one does; the bundle cap decides only how many blocks it arrives in, never whether it goes. Exactly at 80% takes the whole path, because R28 says "80% or more".

`split_whole` takes cues in order into bundle-sized parts and **never splits a cue**. One whose own projected tokens exceed the cap becomes a part on its own and exceeds it — `pack_bundles` already gives an over-cap block a bundle to itself, so it stays visible in the projection as the outsized thing it is, rather than being cut mid-sentence or dropped. The parts partition the cues, and the arithmetic says so exactly: `sum(len(block.text)) == transcript_characters(transcript) - (part_count - 1)`, one joining space consumed at each split.

`excerpt.py` gains `transcript_text`, the ONE definition of the single-space join, with `transcript_characters` defined as its length rather than re-joining. Two separate joins would drift by a space per cue, and the ratio's denominator would then disagree with the whole path's own text about the same transcript. `Excerpt` gains `form`, `part` and `part_count`, all defaulted, so every existing construction site is untouched.

`commands/estimate.py` routes each video **after** the merge and **after** the cap. That order is the requirement, not an implementation detail: measuring before the merge counts every overlapping second twice and pushes nearly everything over the line; measuring before the cap routes a video whole on excerpts that were then thrown away.

### Blind test authorship

`Blind-Tests: capped-whole-transcript-path-1`. **156 test cases** in the two files the plan names, written by a separate agent in a worktree pinned to this pull request's base commit, from the plan alone.

It proved them against a throwaway reference implementation under **20 deliberate mutations**, one at a time — routing on size, strict `>` at the threshold, measuring before the cap, measuring before the merge, zero-based parts, splitting a cue to fit, dropping the last part, joining parts with no space, canonicals from the first excerpt only, a span guessing past the last cue, tokens of the joined text, two joins that drift, `part_count` pinned to 1, closing a part one cue early, unsorted canonicals, an unguarded division by zero, `excerpt_characters` zeroed on the whole path, reversed parts, excerpt blocks marked whole, and a part starting at the video's first cue. Every one failed the tests that name it and no others. Several are discriminating rather than blanket: the strict-`>` mutation failed exactly the two threshold tests and nothing else.

**All 156 passed against this implementation on the first run, with no changes to either side.** That is worth stating plainly because it has not happened before in this session — the previous five slices each turned up a real defect in my code.

### One place the plan is self-contradictory, found independently by both agents

Slice 1's last bullet says `commands/estimate.py` "passes the submissions to `project` alongside the bundles — slice 3's signature". But `project` is `project(bundles, selections, config)`, and `src/find_best_mobo/estimate.py` is **slice 3's file**, not slice 1's. Built literally, slice 1 changes a function it is not allowed to touch and breaks the `estimate` command.

The blind author hit this from the plan alone and resolved it the same way I did: keep the existing three-argument call, and leave the submissions for slice 3 to thread through. Its end-to-end tests assert only that `run()` returns 0 and writes the right bundles, so they do not pin the wrong signature either way.

This is the same shape as the `fetch_all` mistake in R1013, where I changed a signature the plan scoped to another slice and had to revert it.

### Two smaller ambiguities the blind author named

- **`excerpt_characters` on the whole path** is undefined by the plan. It chose the ratio's numerator — the video's excerpts as measured, regardless of path — and pinned it in exactly one test. I chose the same independently. If that reading is wrong, one test names it.
- **`choose_submission` and a missing transcript.** The plan says such a video takes the excerpt path, but the signature is `transcript: Transcript`, not `Transcript | None`. The command handles the missing case before routing, so the parameter stays non-optional.

### Verified locally

1411 passing (156 new). `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean over the whole tree. `mypy src tests` clean over 45 files. `plan-resolve.sh` resolves this plan. `blind-tests.sh` reports every blind-written test unmodified since its authoring commit. `acceptance-criteria.sh` green.

`git diff origin/<base> --stat` is exactly the plan's Files list — six files, nothing else.
